correctness.rationale: On cyclic Markov Q=P−I, truncating exp gives coefficients c_{p,n,r}=sum_{j<=p,j≡r mod n} h^j E_{p−j}(−h)/j!. All are nonnegative for h∈[0,1]. For n>=p and p>=2, unique coefficient h^(p−1)(1−h)/(p−1)! is negative for every h>1; p=1 similarly. The three short-cycle exceptions have unique algebraic boundaries: (p,n)=(3,2) root 2h³−3h²+3h−3; (4,2) root h³−2h²+3h−3; (4,3) root h⁴−4h²+8h−8. Their other coefficients stay nonnegative and monotonicity excludes later reentry. For an arbitrary two-state Markov Q, projector decomposition gives R4(hQ)=Π+E4(−hλ)(I−Π), with E4(−x)>0; entrywise nonnegativity iff its nonstationary eigenvalue lies in the unit disk. At n=3,h=3/2 the exact coefficient vector (−1,39,90)/128 has negative diagonal but spectral radius 79/128. Independent Fraction arithmetic checked 192 (n,p,h) combinations and exact spectral witness; these supplement the coefficient proof.
